title: Are our cellphones "forcing" us to Mall World?

classification.theory_summary: Speculates that frequent exposure to phones/online shopping/ads and sleeping near phones may influence recurring 'Mall World' dreams and their nostalgic/familiar feeling.
classification.skip_reason: No specific dream narrative, locations visited, sensory details, entities, or events are described; the post is speculative/theoretical.

meta.author_theory: Phones are described as a 'mall' with stores/restaurants/entertainment and constant ads; the author wonders if sleeping near phones and being pressured into 'buy mode' influences why people visit 'Mall World' in sleep and why it feels nostalgic/familiar.

extraction.extraction_notes: Post references Mall World generally (e.g., 'nostalgic & familiar feeling', 'don't always buy things') but provides no concrete dream scenes or phenomenological descriptors (light, layout, entities, transitions) that can be extracted as locations/interactions.
